recipes.name: Cinco de Chili Chocolate Cupcakes with Chili Cream Cheese Frosting
ingredients_raw: 1 (18.25 ounce) box devil's food chocolate cake mix
4 cups confectioners' sugar, or more as needed
0.5 teaspoon clear vanilla extract, or to taste

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Line 24 muffin cups with paper liners.

Whisk cake mix, 1 1/2 teaspoons ground ancho chile, and 1/4 teaspoon cayenne pepper. Beat in water, vegetable oil, and eggs with an electric mixer on medium speed; beat for 2 minutes. Spoon batter into the prepared muffin cups, filling them 2/3 full.
Bake in the preheated oven until a toothpick inserted into the center of a cupcake comes out clean, 18 to 22 minutes. Remove and cool completely before frosting.

Sift 1 teaspoon ground ancho chile, 1/8 teaspoon cayenne pepper, and cinnamon with confectioners’ sugar in a mixing bowl. Beat in cream cheese and butter with an electric mixer on medium speed until smooth; mix in vanilla extract.
Spread frosting onto cooled cupcakes in attractive swirls. Poke a small dried chile, stem-side up, into frosting as a garnish.

raw_recipe.headline: Cinco de Chili Chocolate Cupcakes with Chili Cream Cheese Frosting
raw_recipe.description: These dark chocolate chili cakes have the zing and deep, rich flavor of dried ancho chile and cayenne pepper. They are frosted with a chili-flavored cream cheese frosting, and each cupcake is decorated with a cute dried chili on top.

review.reviewBody: Fantastic!!! Love, love, LOVE this recipe! The ancho and cayenne work wonderfully with the richness of the devil's food cake. As written, I found it to have just the right amount of kick - not overwhelming at all. It really is a great 'adult' cupcake. The frosting is KILLER and compliments the cupcakes perfectly. I will definitely make these again. Thanks! :)

I followed the recipe exactly. The frosting was amazing. The cupcake itself had minimal heat. To add extra heat I made a chocolate ganache with 1/3 cup heavy whipping cream and 1 cup milk chocolate chips. To the ganache I added almost 3tsp. Ancho chili pepper powder and about 1.5 tsp Ceyenne pepper. I heavy drizzled it over the icing and what a difference! I got rave reviews and will definitely be making more soon!

Wow! These are great! Per the other reviewers I doubled the spice in the cupcakes and in the frosting. I used my favorite scratch cake recipe and I used Ancho and California Chili spice with the cayenne with a 1/4 tsp of salt. They are for a Potluck tomorrow, but luckily I made extra since my husband is trying to eat them all!

I thought these were a nice change from the usual chocolate cupcakes. I used a homemade chocolate cake (and added cinnamon to it in addition to the other spices), instead of a boxed one. I also agree with other reviewers who added more spices to the cake and frosting--I love that added kick! The only thing I didn't have were the dried red chilis. Maybe next time! Thanks so much for the recipe!

These are awesome!! As suggested by Candice and others, I upped the Ancho Chili to 2 tsp, cayenne to 1/2 and added 2 tsp cinnamon. Left the frosting 'as is' tho only made 3/4 recipe as others suggested. Ended up having to make more. I think if you pipe the icing it uses more than if you just slather it on. Recipe made almost 50 mini cupcakes. This is a keeper! Thanks for sharing Candice.

I made a GF version but I'm going to rate this anyway because this is really two recipes in one. I used a "from scratch" GF dark chocolate cupcake adding the ancho and the cayenne as in the instructions. I made the frosting and thought it needed to be spicier, but I like spice. I made these for a group of people so I made some fire hot and some not. In the tweaked version I tripled the ancho and quadrupled the cayenne but I also fiddled with the cream cheese amount. I wouldn't change the cupcake amounts, they bake up zingy enough. The frosting at first was too sweet for me and so I added more cream cheese to balance it out. Once I had let it sit for a while in the fridge, it became more mellow and so I suggest making this as written, wait and let the flavours meld, then make any adjustments. I think I was too hasty to change the frosting immediately. The outcome though, is a delicious double whammy recipe because both are wonderful on their own, and together they were the hands down winner at my get together. Everyone asked for the recipe. I even used the extra frosting as a filling for crepes....yummmm....Thank you Candice for sharing your recipe!
Good recipe. But if want spicer simmer dried chiles in the water for 15 min then let cool. Use the water as directed in the cake batter. It activates true heat of peppers and really gives a kick.

This was ok, and certainly different. I've had chilli chocolate before and loved it, but these cupcakes weren't quite as good. Needs to be more dark chocolatey I think. I found half the amount of sugar in the icing was quite sufficient, and I prefer my cream cheese icing without butter - the butter doesn't add anything but calories to it. I'm not likely to make these again, but I am glad I gave them a go.

I didn't use a box mix either, I used the recipe for Devils Food Cake I on this site.I also used chocolate pudding, and Patrón Incendio, and substituted Mexican chocolate for the unsweetened chocolate in the recipe. The cupcakes turned out really moist and really rich, and I'm totally addicted to this frosting now.

This is my recipe and I was requested to make 50 for an event in Eugene. I amped up the Ancho and Cayenne ground pepper per request to two teaspoons Ancho and 1/2 teaspoon Cayenne in the CC batter. Actually, I thought it tasted good and was still not too hot for this wimp. That's why I like this recipe. Make it as you like... less pepper powder or more. Of course I made some for hubby too! He liked the spicer version too.

This was the 2nd time I've made these and they were a hit each time. I followed the recipe exactly and the heat is subtle enough for all to enjoy. You could add a bit more chili powder or Cayenne pepper but be careful. I made mini cupcakes - baking 12 minutes - and made 48. Perfect for a dessert tray with bite size treats. Big hit. This recipe is a keeper!

So I made the devil's food from scratch and used olive oil instead of vegetable oil. They turned out well, and i plan on making them again and adding even more heat to them. The combo of heat and chocolate was a hit with the family.

I like cupcakes, but the title amazed me and made me curious to check it out—cupcakes with chili, how? After reading the whole recipe, I was compelled to try it at home. It's the best, and I would recommend it to anyone who wants to give it a try.

We just returned from a Chili Cook-off at our church. I made chili and these cupcakes. Before the voting results were announced, the pastor said, "First of all.... I want to recognize all the praises that were for those Chili Cupcakes. They were wonderful!!" So there it is. Not able to be voted on, but earned great responses from the church. And Yes. They are scrumptious!! I made them exactly per recipe. BUT I didn't put the dried red pepper on top because I was afraid of small children having bad results with them. Everything else was exactly as written.
Have made these several times. Never a crumb left.

Tried out this receipe before bringing to a get together food challenge. My secret ingredient was spicy. I added chopped dried chili's to the frosting for more of a kick. These cupcakes are sooooooo gooood! Will definitely be baking these again.
These were yum. I only used the cupcake part of this recipe, then did a cream cheese and chocolate frosting. The family enjoyed and we liked the chili hit in the cupcake.
Made this twice this weekend, they were delicious! Spices not overpowering, just gave it enough of a kick!
Doubled the spices. Might triple next time!
